statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, was orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress rises a notch to 74 in the high band because Yemen's Houthis have now formally claimed the strike on an Aramco facility near Riyadh with ballistic missiles and drones and warned they would answer escalation with escalation, Saudi aircraft were reported to have hit Sanaa 26 times, and Aramco and Saudi authorities have still confirmed no damage, outage or export impact. Confidence holds at 85 on independently re-verified session levels and ranges, H.15 yields, Trading Economics oil settlements, an attributed rather than anonymous escalation claim and a corroborated seven-day calendar, offset by the continuing absence of any live price path.
recommendation: Tail stays in the low band for the first 21 scored hours, so the deterministic mapping remains EA_ON and green through 21:00Z. The three reopening hours from 22:00Z carry Tail 21, 23 and 21, which maps to WATCH and yellow: that is the mildest cautionary band and reflects a dated discontinuity meeting thin Sunday-evening liquidity while a claimed missile and drone strike on Saudi refining capacity is still unquantified. The Saudi cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z is the only live venue with direct exposure to that strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or the current action. A narrow danger window is published across the three reopening hours as a dated discontinuity checkpoint. The next scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, with FOMC minutes on 7 October.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while a now formally claimed Houthi missile and drone strike on an Aramco site near Riyadh lifts Stress to 74 and moves the three hours after the 22:00Z Sunday restart into the watch band
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels were independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is unchanged: the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2% against 4.1% expected, monthly wage growth slowed to 0.1% and annual wage growth to 3.0%. Equities read that as cementing a Fed hold at the 28 October meeting, but the curve did not follow. The 2-year finished at 4.8414%, up 5.44 basis points, and the 10-year at 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points, so a soft labour print was met with a higher long end. The Federal Reserve H.15 release has published only through 1 October, where the 2-year stands at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's reversal is carried from market reporting rather than from the official series.

The material change since the previous hour is attribution. Yemen's Houthis have now formally claimed the strike on an Aramco facility near Riyadh: military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group used ballistic missiles and drones, that the operation achieved its objective and ignited fires at the targeted sites, and warned the group would answer blockade with blockade and escalation with escalation. Reuters and AFP journalists separately observed flames and smoke rising from the Aramco refinery south of Riyadh on Saturday afternoon. In the other direction, Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah reported 26 Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa, correspondents there reported warplanes firing on the city, and the Houthis claimed 94 strikes against areas under their control within 24 hours. What remains unverified is the part that matters most for markets: neither Aramco nor Saudi authorities have confirmed that the facility was attacked, and no damage assessment, outage or export impact has been published. The claim upgrades an anonymous incident into a reciprocal escalation chain between named belligerents, which is why Stress moves from 72 to 74, but an unquantified strike is not evidence of a pathological Nasdaq-100 price path, so Tail does not follow it.

Energy remains the transmission channel. WTI settled at $91.11, down 1.90%, after trading to a one-month low of $88.06 intraday, while Brent closed at $102.25, essentially unchanged on the day and still up 58.45% year on year. The divergence is the story: futures softened on the G7 and IEA agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and other emergency reserves over four months, while Dated Brent traded above $120 on a record physical distillate squeeze. A strike on refining capacity lands directly on that squeeze. The Strait of Hormuz has been largely blocked since 28 February 2026, although September LNG transits reached their highest monthly level since the conflict began, at 19 cargoes. The OPEC+ participating countries meet online on 4 October to set November policy and a rollover at September levels is widely expected; because the exact hour is not reliably published it is carried as a driver checkpoint rather than a dated calendar event.

The window has advanced and so has its shape. Twenty-one of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them, and Tail is held between 3 and 18 across that stretch. The restart at 22:00Z on 4 October, the first full trading hour at 23:00Z and the second at 00:00Z on 5 October now carry Tail 21, 23 and 21, which crosses the 20 threshold into the watch band for the first time this weekend. That step reflects a combination the previous hours did not have: a dated discontinuity at a known instant, a claimed strike on refining capacity whose damage is unassessed, an explicit threat of further escalation, an already-squeezed distillate market and thin Sunday-evening liquidity that mechanically widens the reopening distribution. It is deliberately narrow, covering three hours rather than a session, and it remains the mildest cautionary band. A gap alone would not confirm Tail; a gap followed by shallow or failed retracements and repeated extension would be the first genuine Tail evidence of the week, and an Aramco confirmation of limited damage would make these three slots too cautious rather than too low.

The week ahead is moderate on U.S. macro: ISM Services on Monday, the trade balance, Williams and Bowman speeches and a 3-year auction on Tuesday, FOMC minutes and a 10-year auction on Wednesday, jobless claims and a 30-year auction on Thursday, and preliminary Michigan sentiment on Friday, with the next rate decision not until 28 October. The shared Finviz context was again unusable for this run: it was collected on 29 September, roughly 98 hours old against the 90-minute freshness bound, and is marked partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable. The evidence failed open exactly as the contract requires and the assessment rests entirely on independent research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments and no slot required an unavailable entry. The window opens at 01:00Z on 3 October with Tail 9 and Stress 66 under a normal mode and decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 9 to 3 by 12:00Z and stays at 3 for the remaining thirteen hours. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z and then climbs steadily to 72 by 00:00Z on 4 October as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and produced the strike on the Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 80 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. No historical opinion was revised.
outlookSummary: Twenty-one of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 06:00Z, ticks up across the Saudi cash session, then rises along the restart approach to 18 by 21:00Z, mapping to EA_ON and green for those 21 hours. The three reopening hours from 22:00Z carry Tail 21, 23 and 21, crossing into the watch band and mapping to WATCH and yellow on a dated discontinuity, thin opening liquidity and an unquantified claimed strike on Saudi refining capacity. Stress runs from 74 to a peak of 79 and stays in the high band before easing to 75 once a venue can price the weekend's news. Confidence eases from 85 to a low of 77 before the restart as Friday's levels age, lifts during the Saudi session and recovers to 85 once live prices return. The dominant mode shifts to mixed four hours before the restart on two-sided catalysts rather than any observed directional bias, becomes event/whipsaw across the discontinuity and returns to mixed. A narrow danger window marks the three reopening hours.
